name: Shaily Engineering Plastics Ltd
tagline: High-precision injection-moulder that has become a picks-and-shovels supplier of GLP-1 pen injector devices to 23-24 global pharma partners ahead of the semaglutide patent cliff - exceptional returns profile (ROCE 29-42%, ROE 27-33%) but already a ~Rs 14,000 Cr mid-cap trading rich, with a genuine oral-GLP-1 cannibalisation debate and recent promoter selling
business_overview: Vadodara-based contract manufacturer of injection-moulded precision plastic components and sub-assemblies across three segments - Consumer (IKEA-anchored homeware, ~55% of revenue, slow-growing), Healthcare (drug-delivery devices, the growth engine) and Industrial. The Healthcare vertical makes IP-led pen injectors / auto-injectors for GLP-1 drugs (generic semaglutide/tirzepatide) and has ~23-24 global pharma partners lined up for patent expiries in India, Canada and Brazil (from 2026). Pen capacity being scaled 80M -> 150M/year, plus a ~Rs 300 Cr Abu Dhabi medical-device facility (75M pens, live Q4FY28). Early work on consumer-electronics and semiconductor precision components as a further leg. (Source: trusted-x, @unseenvalue dedicated single-stock writeup, non-negative tone, first_seen 2026-09-07; scan tier 4.55, no conviction floor.)
fundamentals_table: Q2FY26 +34% YoY, Q3FY26 +27% YoY (9M +32%); Healthcare +163% YoY in Q2FY26
Q2FY26 gross 59.3%, EBITDA 31.8% (vs 21.5% YoY), PAT +134% YoY
Rich; UBS initiated Buy Dec-25 with Rs 4,000 TP citing 96% Healthcare revenue CAGR FY25-28
fundamentals_narrative: Still one of the cleanest return profiles in the screen on trailing numbers (ROCE ~29%, FY26 PAT +82.5%), but the primary-filings deep-dive surfaces a real, recent deceleration the prior pass didn't have: Q1FY27 revenue grew only +14% YoY (vs 27-34% in the three prior quarters), with the Consumer segment (still ~49% of sales) declining 24% on weak European/US demand. Healthcare still grew 85% and is now 51% of sales, and management points to commodity/freight cost timing (guided to normalise by Q3FY27) rather than a structural reset - but at ~85x trailing PE (a 458% premium to the peer median), the multiple is priced for the OLD growth regime, not the new one. A promoter-group member (Vanita L Nagda) sold her entire 2.27% stake the same quarter, though with nil pledge/encumbrance this reads as a personal liquidity event, not a leveraged exit. Balance sheet remains comfortable (D/E 0.3x) and a first dividend was initiated in May-2026.
technical_read: Not pulled - the assessment turns on valuation and the oral-pill debate, not on chart position; near 52-week high is already known.
sentiment_summary: 277-post thread, most recent post 2026-06-29. Community is broadly constructive on the GLP-1 device opportunity but with an active, high-quality bear debate: oral semaglutide/orforglipron cannibalising injectables, India generic GLP-1 offtake being slower than expected (Nithin Kamath / press cited), and promoter stake sale flagged as a worry in the last two posts. Bulls (BuyRightSitTight, nil_71, idikasony, rajvinder.singh - a 7-year holder calling management 'honest and conservative') frame Shaily as a classic picks-and-shovels play where the device is needed regardless of which pharma wins, and note OneSource is fully booked. UBS Buy (Rs 4,000) and Capital Group bulk-buying (Mar-26) are external validation.
community_signal: No core-tier (phreakv6) call. Marathondreams (elevated) posted factual competitive-landscape updates (Zydus single-pen device) without a directional call. General tenor from long-term holders is positive-but-watchful. The @unseenvalue Substack writeup that seeded this (trusted-x, 'high' strength) is an analytical piece framed around whether Shaily's edge is 'specific knowledge or a patent', non-negative.

value_chain.position: Device / drug-delivery layer - makes the pen injectors and auto-injectors that generic semaglutide/tirzepatide players need; sits between the API/fill-finish companies (e.g. OneSource, DRL) and the branded/generic marketers. Complementary to fill-finish, not competing with it.
value_chain.pricing_power: Moderate - IP-led / patented pen designs and regulated-market device qualification give some pricing power and stickiness, but multiple global device makers exist and large innovators could in-source; margins so far protected by mix and scarcity of Indian precision-moulding capacity
value_chain.bottleneck_exposure: Positive - injectable GLP-1 volume growth and the 2026+ patent cliff create a device-supply pull; the risk is the bottleneck easing if oral formulations take share from injectables

four_box.note: Strong GLP-1 device tailwind and TAM, real precision-moulding moat, but valuation is rich near the 52-week high; score permits a return-magnitude label which judgment declines to apply given ~Rs 14,000 Cr size and the oral-pill risk

deep_dive.conviction_update: Medium -> Low-Medium. The primary filings confirm real deceleration (Q1FY27 revenue +14% vs 27-34% in the prior three quarters) plus a genuine Consumer-segment decline (-24%), landing on top of an already-rich ~85x trailing multiple and a promoter-group stake exit in the same quarter. None of these are disqualifying on their own (management flags a plausible commodity-cost explanation, no pledge, no red flag), but stacked together they are a net-negative update against a thesis that was already held to 'neither' on valuation grounds.
